steps.name: Strandedness risk and count-integrity assessment
caveats: The gene matrix is pre-filtered to ~12000 genes, so at-risk fractions are computed over this matrix, not over the whole transcriptome
This step cannot determine the actual strandedness setting used at counting — only quantify exposure
steps.context: Same count matrix as T1S1 (12000 genes, human). Use EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 (installed) to get gene coordinates and strand; overlap logic via GenomicRanges. The count file is gene-level only — no transcript or per-read strand information exists, so strandedness can only be bounded, not recovered.
steps.question: How much of the count matrix could be corrupted by an unknown/wrong strandedness setting at featureCounts, and can treated-vs-control DE proceed safely on gene-level counts?
steps.description: Because strandedness was never recorded, reads from overlapping genes on opposite strands could have been mis-assigned at the featureCounts stage, and a wrong -s setting can silently corrupt counts. Using human gene coordinates and strands from the installed EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 annotation, identify genes in the count matrix that overlap an antisense neighbor (sense/antisense pairs, including completely bidirectional loci), then quantify what fraction of matrix genes and of total mapped counts sit in such at-risk pairs. Report the verdict: if at-risk counts are a small fraction, proceed to DE with a caveat; if large, flag which DE hits could be strand artifacts. Optionally compare count distributions of at-risk vs safe genes for anomalies.

steps.name: Differential expression: DESeq2 with edgeR and voom concordance
caveats: Any gene flagged at-risk in T1S2 that reaches significance must be marked as possibly a strand artifact
Report optimistic-vs-concordant status: genes found by only one of the three models are candidate, not confirmed
steps.context: Design ~ condition (treated vs control), n=3 per arm, unpaired, single batch — no covariates available in the 6x2 metadata. With 3 vs 3, expect wide confidence intervals; report effect sizes with uncertainty rather than FDR alone. The folder name suggests a multi-model evaluation: DESeq2 (negative binomial), edgeR (quasi-likelihood), and limma-voom (linear model) are the three standard count-model frameworks available here.
steps.question: Which genes differ between the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples, and which of those differences are robust to the choice of count-based statistical model?
steps.description: Primary analysis with DESeq2: filter low-count genes, size-factor normalization, design ~condition, Wald test, BH FDR, and apeglm LFC shrinkage for ranking. Run edgeR quasi-likelihood and limma-voom on the same filtered matrix as sensitivity analyses; compare hit lists across the three models and report concordant genes (found by all three) separately from model-specific ones. Outputs: full results tables, volcano plot, heatmap of top genes, and a concordant-signature list for enrichment.

edgeR and limma-voom results tables from the same filtered matrix and design

Gene IDs in the count matrix must be reconciled to HGNC symbols (or Entrez) before matching; if gene identifiers are not symbols, map via the available human ID-mapping resource and report unmapped fraction.

steps.description: Run fgsea against WikiPathways human gene sets (HGNC symbols, provisioned under /mnt/refs) using the full ranked list (shrunken log2FC from DESeq2), plus over-representation of the concordant-gene shortlist from T1S3. Report pathways enriched in treated vs control with NES, FDR, and leading-edge genes. If the human gene set resource is unavailable, report the gap and output the ranked list for later use.

Results table with pathway, NES, p, FDR; both enriched directions reported
Leading-edge genes named for top pathways

plan.title: Liver 3v3 drug-treatment DE with count QC and strandedness check
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a small human liver bulk RNA-seq experiment (counts.csv: 12000 genes x 6 samples of raw STAR/featureCounts integer counts; metadata.csv: 6 x 2 with a condition column defining 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch). Two facts shape the plan: (1) the user doubts the counts, and (2) library strandedness was never recorded, so a wrong strand setting at the featureCounts stage could have mis-assigned reads on overlapping genes. The plan therefore first validates the counts (sample alignment, library sizes, PCA/clustering to flag outliers, and a liver-marker plausibility check), then bounds the strandedness risk by identifying genes in the count matrix that overlap an antisense neighbor using the installed human EnsDb annotation — if at-risk genes carry a small share of counts, gene-level DE is safe; if large, hits overlapping those genes are flagged. Differential expression then runs with DESeq2 (primary, with apeglm shrinkage) on design ~condition with 3 vs 3, plus edgeR quasi-likelihood and limma-voom on the same filtered matrix as sensitivity analyses; genes found by all three models are reported as the robust signature, and any hit falling in the at-risk antisense-overlap set is annotated as possibly strand-artifact. The signature is finally contextualized with fgsea against the provisioned WikiPathways human GMT. With 3 vs 3 the power is limited, so concordance across models and effect sizes, not FDR alone, drive the conclusions.
